title: Building the Function: The Auxiliary-Function Trick
quickIdea: When the conclusion names a point where something vanishes, build the function whose derivative is that something, check its two endpoint values, then quote Rolle.
remember: The mean value theorem itself is Rolle applied to g(x) = f(x) - [f(a) + ((f(b) - f(a))/(b - a))(x - a)], the vertical gap between the curve and its chord. g(a) = g(b) = 0.
For 'show ax^2 + bx + c = 0 has a root in (0, 1) given 2a + 3b + 6c = 0', integrate: F(x) = ax^3/3 + bx^2/2 + cx has F(0) = 0 and F(1) = (2a + 3b + 6c)/6 = 0, and F' is the given quadratic.
The recipe: read the object that must vanish, integrate it, verify the two endpoint values, then apply Rolle to the integral.
Always check both endpoint values before quoting the theorem; a construction that does not give equal endpoints proves nothing.
Cauchy's theorem uses the same construction with h(x) = (f(b) - f(a)) g(x) - (g(b) - g(a)) f(x).

example.prompt: If 2a + 3b + 6c = 0, show that ax^2 + bx + c = 0 has at least one root in (0, 1).
example.work: Let F(x) = ax^3/3 + bx^2/2 + cx. Then F(0) = 0 and F(1) = a/3 + b/2 + c = (2a + 3b + 6c)/6 = 0, so F satisfies Rolle's hypotheses on [0, 1] and some c0 in (0, 1) has F'(c0) = 0. But F'(x) = ax^2 + bx + c.
example.answer: There is a root of ax^2 + bx + c in (0, 1), namely the Rolle point of F.

gateAngle: This is the shape of the descriptive MVT questions in the older GATE papers and of the 'which of the following must be true' statement questions: the given relation between the coefficients is exactly the equal-endpoint condition of some integral.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: If f(0) = 0 and f(1) = 1, show that some c in (0, 1) has f'(c) = 2c.
variations.answer: Apply Rolle to g(x) = f(x) - x^2.
variations.why: g(0) = 0 - 0 = 0 and g(1) = 1 - 1 = 0, so Rolle gives g'(c) = 0, that is f'(c) - 2c = 0. The auxiliary function is read off the conclusion: the thing that must vanish is f'(x) - 2x, so integrate it to get f(x) - x^2.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why does the mean value theorem need an auxiliary function at all, when Rolle's theorem is enough?
variations.answer: Because Rolle needs equal endpoint values, and the chord is what makes them equal.
variations.why: Subtracting the chord removes the height difference between f(a) and f(b), so the gap function starts and ends at 0 - and its derivative is f' minus the average slope.

trap.what: Applying Rolle to the given function instead of to its integral.
trap.why: The given quadratic has no reason to take equal values at the endpoints; the relation between the coefficients is a condition on the integral.
trap.counterexample: For a = 1, b = 0, c = -1/3 the relation 2a + 3b + 6c = 2 - 2 = 0 holds, and x^2 - 1/3 is not equal at 0 and 1 - Rolle cannot be applied to it, yet its root 0.577 does lie in (0, 1).

check.question: If f(0) = f(1) = f(2) = 0, how many distinct zeros does f' have in (0, 2)?
check.explanation: Rolle on [0, 1] gives one zero in (0, 1) and Rolle on [1, 2] gives another in (1, 2); the two intervals are disjoint, so the zeros are distinct.
